scopeNotes: Three imported island records share this geographic history. Independent statehood begins in 1979, not at a map snapshot boundary. Matching footprints were inspected; exact geometry remains unverified.

The 2002 archaeological report was read in selected field and discussion passages. Modern excavation dates do not date ancient occupation. Pottery styles are not treated as ethnic replacements; uncertain shell scoop identifications remain qualified.
The colonial collection introduction is used for broad chronology. Conflicting precise dates for first French settlement are avoided by an approximate mid-seventeenth-century phase.

French revolutionary emancipation and British re-enslavement are distinguished from 1834 abolition and the 1838 end of compulsory apprenticeship. A commemorative government article collapsing freedom into 1838 was not followed.

Phulgence’s selected chapter-four passages and interviews support the resistance and memorial discussion. The full thesis was not independently reviewed. Troop counts and assertions that the 1796 fighters already represented an independent nation are omitted.
The 1832 order is a colonial prescription accessed through UNB’s transcription, not proof of compliance. Its exact calendar day is uncertain.
Constitutional history is used for historical phases only. Associated-statehood day discrepancies are avoided; the original independence order verifies 22 February 1979.
Flower festivals are not labelled UNESCO-inscribed: preparatory nomination assistance is not inscription. The Folk Research Centre identifies their precise origins as unknown.

Nobel materials support individual contributions, not a claim of uniform educational opportunity. The Walcott transcript was read; interview video was not independently played. Bibliographic errors in an alternative Nobel biography are not used.
No successor links are invented between island snapshots. Independent historical review and depth certification remain pending.
